headword: {大衆文学|たいしゅうぶんがく}

definitions.gloss: popular fiction; mass-market literature; entertainment literature
definitions.explanation: Literature aimed at a broad general audience for entertainment, as opposed to highbrow or literary fiction. Includes genres such as mystery, historical fiction, romance, and adventure.

examples.japanese: {大衆文学|たいしゅうぶんがく}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{幅広|はばひろ}い→幅広い：11326_habahiroi⟧⟦{読者|どくしゃ}→読者：16554_dokusha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{親|した}しまれている→親しむ：14139_shitashimu⟧。
examples.english: Popular fiction is enjoyed by a wide range of readers.

examples.japanese: ⟦{推理小説|すいりしょうせつ}→推理小説：28077_suirishousetsu⟧や{時代小説|じだいしょうせつ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{大衆文学|たいしゅうぶんがく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{分類|ぶんるい}される→分類する：25224_bunruisuru⟧。
examples.english: Mystery novels and period novels are classified as popular fiction.

examples.english: The boundary between literary fiction and popular fiction has become increasingly blurred over the years.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japanese literary circles, {大衆文学|たいしゅうぶんがく} is distinguished from ⟦{純文学|じゅんぶんがく}→純文学：13983_junbungaku⟧ (literary fiction). The ⟦{直木賞|なおきしょう}→直木賞：15560_naokishou⟧ (Naoki Prize) is awarded for the best work of popular fiction, while the ⟦{芥川賞|あくたがわしょう}→芥川賞：15559_akutagawashou⟧ (Akutagawa Prize) is for literary fiction. Major authors include {松本清張|まつもとせいちょう} and {東野圭吾|ひがしのけいご}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大衆文学|たいしゅうぶんがく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{作家|さっか}→作家：01414_sakka⟧ (popular fiction writer)
- {大衆文学|たいしゅうぶんがく}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{純文学|じゅんぶんがく}→純文学：13983_junbungaku⟧ (popular fiction and literary fiction)

- ⟦{純文学|じゅんぶんがく}→純文学：13983_junbungaku⟧: literary fiction — works focused on artistic expression rather than entertainment
